tagline: Named for a fiddle tune, and it twists like one.
intro: Out of Black Mountain, NC 9 runs south past the I-40 interchange and into sharp curves and hairpin turns, some seventeen miles of them, down to the hamlet of Bat Cave. There it picks up US 64 and US 74A and goes on through Hickory Nut Gorge, past Chimney Rock, to Lake Lure, where the byway ends. A spur runs west on US 64 to Edneyville.

The name comes from an old fiddle tune, and the state's guidebook says the road plays it, all twists and turns and ups and downs. The Black Mountains got their own name from the dark green firs that cover them.

moments.title: Bat Cave
moments.text: Named for a granite fissure cave on Bluerock Mountain that is closed to the public, the hamlet on the Broad River keeps losing its road signs, especially around the time of Batman Returns.

moments.title: Chimney Rock
moments.text: Between Bat Cave and Chimney Rock village the road passes below a 315-foot gneiss monolith, and in the state park around it Hickory Nut Falls drops 404 feet.

moments.title: Lake Lure
moments.text: The Morse family dammed the Broad River to make the lake in the 1920s, lost it to a Philadelphia mortgage holder in the Depression, and the town bought the dam and lake in 1965.
